findings.text: non-blocking: the manifest is parsed unconditionally, where the promotion this docstring claims to mirror goes through _fresh_manifest (promotion_checks.py:451) and fills nothing from a manifest whose mtime does not postdate the pointer's manifest_baseline_mtime_ns, so for a stale manifest the remedy names a log the promotion never reads and asks for an EXIT=<n> record in it while the repair the coordinator actually owes (rewriting the manifest for this attempt) goes unnamed.

non-blocking: the first-test_logs-entry selection is written a second time here rather than taken from promotion_records.py:338, so if the promotion's fill changes which entry it reads the remedy names a different log and the coordinator edits the wrong file.

non-blocking: the assertion reads refused["guard"] against MISSING_EXIT_STATUS_GUARD, the literal the test supplies to _land at line 165, so it holds whatever land_once does with the guard and survives a regression in the remedy it was added beside.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against b4ec6217eb — 8105ae004f adds _landing_remedy and its helpers to queue_landing.py plus a remedy append in obligations.py:1164, and aab4155481 adds the evidence fragment; 338 insertions and 7 deletions across four files, all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_a_landing_refusal_names_its_remedy.py with two cases (the row names the log and the missing record; the quoted exit form is still refused); both are present at lines 154 and 188 and the manifest records the gate run as 2 passed.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a landing refusal names its remedy; plan §27 states it for a gate log lacking a terminal EXIT=<n> record, and reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:440 _landing_remedy derives that sentence from the run's manifest and records it as admission_landing.remedy.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, it records the gate (2 passed), the negative control (1 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1) and both population arms (base 5 failed/487 passed, head 5 failed/489 passed) with their log paths and exit statuses.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares five paths (queue_landing.py, obligations.py, the new test, the evidence fragment, a figures directory); the diff touches four of them and nothing outside them, and the figures directory was correctly left unused.

justifications.durability: the negative control proves tests/test_a_landing_refusal_names_its_remedy.py:182 reddens when the remedy is dropped, though the assertion at line 173 compares a guard the test itself handed to _land and cannot fail.
justifications.evidence: the new test is the done-when's own file and its recorded run is 2 passed in after-node-gate.log, while negative-control.log shows the remedy-free row failing the very assertion that reads the log path and EXIT=<n>.
justifications.fit: queue_landing.py:356-358 follows the module's module-level constant and `#:` comment idiom and every added name states its mechanism, and ruff check reports nothing on the three staged Python paths.
justifications.goal_fidelity: queue_landing.py:404 _gate_check_remedy names the log the manifest cites and the terminal EXIT=<n> record it must end in, and the exit reader it consults (promotion_evidence._recorded_exit_status) is unchanged so the quoted form stays refused.
justifications.reuse: queue_landing.py:368 reuses the owners _manifest_relative_path and _recorded_exit_status, but line 380 re-derives the first-test_logs selection that promotion_records.py:338 already owns and the parse skips the freshness gate at promotion_checks.py:451.
justifications.scope_discipline: the four changed paths are all inside the manifest's declared write paths and the change carries no refactor of the surrounding landing pass.
